title: QuantumShift: Low-Precision Arithmetic for Quantum-Classical Hybrid Systems
problem: Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms require significant classical overhead for data preparation, post-processing, and classical subroutines, which dominates execution time on near-term quantum systems. Reducing this overhead while maintaining algorithm correctness is a critical challenge.
motivation: Efficient hybrid quantum-classical systems are essential for achieving practical quantum advantage, as classical overhead often becomes the bottleneck.
method: QuantumShift introduces low-precision arithmetic schemes specifically designed for hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. The approach carefully reduces numerical precision in classical components while employing techniques to maintain algorithm correctness and convergence properties. The scheme is co-designed to work seamlessly with quantum components, reducing classical overhead without sacrificing algorithm quality.
key_novelty: Low-precision arithmetic tailored for hybrid quantum-classical systems that achieves significant overhead reduction while provably maintaining algorithm correctness.
contributions: Low-precision arithmetic schemes for hybrid quantum-classical algorithms
60% reduction in classical overhead with correctness guarantees
Analysis of precision requirements for maintaining hybrid algorithm convergence
primary_theme: quantum-classical hybrid acceleration through precision reduction
